changes.after: The Committee judges that the case for an increase in the federal funds rate has strengthened but decided, for the time being, to wait for further evidence of continued progress toward its objectives.

changes.before: Near-term risks to the economic outlook have diminished.
changes.after: Near-term risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced.

changes.before: indicates that the labor market strengthened and that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate rate.
changes.after: indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and growth of economic activity has picked up from the modest pace seen in the first half of this year.

changes.before: Voting against the action was Esther L. George, who preferred at this meeting to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/2 to 3/4 percent.
changes.after: Voting against the action were: Esther L. George, Loretta J. Mester, and Eric Rosengren, each of whom preferred at this meeting to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/2 to 3/4 percent.
labor market conditions will strengthen somewhat further.

changes.before: Job gains were strong in June following weak growth in May. On balance, payrolls and other labor market indicators point to some increase in labor utilization in recent months.
changes.after: Although the unemployment rate is little changed in recent months, job gains have been solid, on average.

parsed.rationale: The statement adds explicit language that the case for a rate increase has strengthened, upgrades the growth assessment, and judges risks roughly balanced. Three dissents in favor of a hike signal a near-term tightening bias, though rates were held and the forward guidance was unchanged.

spans.quote: Near-term risks to the economic outlook have diminished.
indicates that the labor market strengthened and that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate rate.
Voting against the action was Esther L. George, who preferred at this meeting to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/2 to 3/4 percent.
Job gains were strong in June following weak growth in May. On balance, payrolls and other labor market indicators point to some increase in labor utilization in recent months.

The Committee judges that the case for an increase in the federal funds rate has strengthened but decided, for the time being, to wait for further evidence of continued progress toward its objectives.
Near-term risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced.
indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and growth of economic activity has picked up from the modest pace seen in the first half of this year.

Voting against the action were: Esther L. George, Loretta J. Mester, and Eric Rosengren, each of whom preferred at this meeting to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/2 to 3/4 percent.
labor market conditions will strengthen somewhat further.
Although the unemployment rate is little changed in recent months, job gains have been solid, on average.
